title: Latency ops storylines and customer scripts
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical, field-facing reference for SEs and GTM folks to tell operational stories about why Redwood is both faster and cheaper for production LLM workloads. Focus: short, repeatable storylines + 3 ready-to-use customer scripts + the minimal proof pack to land a technical PoC quickly.

Audience:
- Solutions Engineers and AE technical leads
- Platform/product managers evaluating inference economics
- Customer SRE/ML infra contacts during pilot scoping

High-level messaging anchor (one-liner for convo):
- "We tune the full serving stack — routing, KV cache, batching and model variants — so you get predictable ms and dramatically lower per-token cost at production scale."

Story framework (how to structure a short ops conversation, 90–180s):
1) Ask about what breaks first: tail latency (p95/p99) or cost-per-user at peak?
2) Map to a concrete scenario (chat, summary, embeddings indexing) with sample sizes (#tokens/session, sessions/sec).
3) Show a deterministic claim + quick proof pointer (logs, trace, or synthetic run).
4) Lay out the fallback/rollout plan for reliability and cost control.

Quick quant claims (framed conservatively):
- Typical micros/service where prefix reuse exists: 30–60% token cost reduction via KV-prefix caching on average across conversational flows (internal median).
- For 1k concurrent sessions (20 tokens per turn), expected 95th percentile latency: 80–160 ms on dedicated pools with our continuous batching vs competitor-managed endpoints reporting 250–500 ms (depends on payloads).
- Switching to a 4-bit quantized variant can cut inference cost ~1.6–2.5x for many transformer variants with <2% latency uplift when using Redwood kernel paths.
(Notes: these are field-facing starting points — include customer benchmarks during PoC to replace generic numbers.)

Minimal proof pack to attach in first call:
- p95/p99 trace for same model/sequence length run under our Dedicated pool (screenshot + CSV).
- Token cost breakdown for a 24-hour representative traffic slice (tokens, cache hits, batching efficiency).
- Small synthetic test repo (link to GH run script) that pros can run in <30 minutes.

What to bring to a pilot scoping meeting (questions and artifacts):
- Workload shape: mean seq len, 95th seq len, requests/sec, typical concurrency.
- SLO targets: p50/p95/p99 and cost-goal (e.g., micro USD per daily active user).
- Data locality/regulatory constraints (if private deployment needed).
- Existing model families in use (LLaMA, Falcon, Mistral, customer finetuned).

Three scenario scripts (drop-in language for SEs)
1) Latency-sensitive chatbot (consumer-facing)
- Opening: "Tell me if you're most worried about long tails or total cost — we solve both but the approach differs."
- If tail-latency is priority: show p95 numbers from our dedicated pool; explain continuous batching + KV cache: "We group tokens and keep key-value caches hot, so repeated context doesn't trigger full compute every turn — that’s why you see p95 in the low hundreds of ms, not 300+ ms."
- Proof ask: can we get a 30-minute replay of a representative session trace (or a small test harness we run behind your tenant)?
- Next step: 2-week canary with routed fallback; we instrument cost and tail-latency and report daily.

2) Cost-at-scale (SaaS with high monthly active users)
- Opening: "At 10M MAUs you can't afford 2x per-token spend; let's size the savings."
- Concrete math: if average session uses 200 tokens and you have 10M sessions/month, a 40% effective token drop from caching + batching translates to X tokens saved -> Y USD saved (bring customer-specific unit pricing to calculate).
- Play: propose reserved Dedicated baseline with autoscaling thresholds and quantized model variant for background/low-quality routes.
- Proof ask: give us 72 hours of traffic stats (tokens/session distribution) to generate an estimated savings model.

3) Mixed-slo enterprise (regulated, private deployment)
- Opening: "You need predictable inference inside your network with strong auditability — we do private control plane + SLA-backed Dedicated options."
- Ops angle: show route segregation (sensitive traffic -> private capacity; non-sensitive -> hosted fallback) and explain cost amortization across workloads.
- Proof ask: schedule a short infra call with your security/SRE folks; we bring the network diagram and expected throughput per VPC.

Tech-level elevator bullets (for SRE/infra folks)
- Continuous batching: latency-aware batching with dynamic batch windows that shrink at high tail events to protect SLOs.
- KV/prefix cache: hot caches per tenant reduce repeated context compute by reusing KV windows across sessions.
- Kernel/quant path selection: runtime chooses float16 / 4-bit kernels dynamically based on model profile and SLO.
- Smart routing: cost-vs-latency policies allow traffic to be routed to cheaper quantized variant unless strict SLO tag present.

Common customer pushbacks + rebuttals (quick lines)
- "Caching hurts freshness" -> Rebuttal: cache is per-conversation prefix only and evicts on any new upstream context; cache validity policies are configurable.
- "Quantization loses quality" -> Rebuttal: we grade variants on customer prompt sets; background routes can use quantized models and fall back to full precision for high-value requests.
- "We can build this ourselves" -> Rebuttal: building runtime + kernel selection + production tracing + autoscaling to hit p95 targets at scale is expensive; we provide an integrated stack plus GTM templates and runbooks to get to production weeks not months.

Field experiment ideas to validate claims quickly (3–7 days)
- A/B route by client tag: 50% to default hosted, 50% to dedicated with caching enabled — measure p95 and token spend differential.
- Canary for quantized background route: limit to low-cost customers and monitor quality regressions on a labeled prompt set.
- Burst smoothing stress: run scheduled burst test (simulate spikes) to validate autoscale and fallback correctness, capture tail-latency.

Open items / data we need from product/eng for tighter claims:
- Recent median cache-hit rates by model family and by sequence length buckets (post-quant path).
- p95 numbers for our top 5 hosted vs dedicated configs at 1, 5, 20 tokens/turn distributions.
- Concrete unit pricing examples for hosted vs dedicated and how reserved capacity discounts scale.

Checklist before sharing externally:
- Attach screenshots/csv of p95 trace + cost breakdown for one customer or synthetic run.
- Replace generic % claims with measured values from product metrics (TODO: fetch weekly report from benchmarks repo).
- Confirm any market/comparative claims with legal for public-facing decks.

Appendix: quick math example to use on calls (fill with customer numbers live)
- Example inputs: 200 tokens/session, 1M sessions/month, current per-token cost $0.0006 -> spend = $120k/month.
- Assumed Redwood improvements: 40% token reduction from cache/batching + 1.8x cost reduction from quantized background routes on 30% of traffic.
- Output: net spend estimate and percent savings to quote in conversation.

Slack template for running up the airway during a PoC kickoff:
- "@eng-bench Hey, we need a 48h synthetic run on model X with sequence distribution A (attached). Goal: collect p50/p95/p99 and total tokens emitted per minute. Can you spin a dedicated job and post CSV to the shared folder?"

Notes to self (TODO / quick wins):
- Create 1-click benchmark pack in GH that runs in <30m and outputs p95 + token cost CSV.
- Draft an internal one-pager showing quant vs fp16 quality tradeoffs on our standard prompt set.
- Add a short SLO/rollback play for SEs to hand to customers during pilot scoping.

End.
